newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates steady, liquidity strained.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates steady, liquidity strained.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were steady on Wednesday amid slightly strained liquidity, dealers said.
"The demand is relatively strong and the supply has shrunk a bit...but the rates have not changed," one dealer said.
Vacations are coming and banks' clients are drawing more cash, the dealer said. Commercial banks' accounts were down 100 million kuna to 486 million on Tuesday.
Commercial banks had 9.25 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans from the central bank, down from Tuesday's 21 million.
Fresh money market loans by 0900 GMT were put at 38 million kuna, of which 17.5 million were call money made at a steady 8.0 percent.
Two-week funds were granted at a stable 11 percent and two-month at 16 percent.

Two banks borrowed 18.5 million kuna in overnight loans on Tuesday, which one used to square its position and the other to maintain its mandatory reserve. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
